summary: Rebecca Rowena Randall, a poor girl selling soap and cakes door to door, pitches a wealthy gentleman on a porch and describes the Simpson family's need for a banquet lamp. Moved by her story, the man orders three hundred cakes, which will give the Simpsons a lamp by Christmas and a shade by summer. Rebecca tips into a lilac bush at the news, then learns his name is Aladdin-like and runs off to tell her friend Emma Jane.
one_line: Rebecca Randall sells soap and cakes to a generous stranger, whose large order will help the Simpson family buy a banquet lamp.
key_facts: Rebecca explains to the man that she is poor but lives with her aunts in a brick house, and that her aunts would not like her to be a peddler.
Rebecca is selling on behalf of friends, describing Mr. Simpson, Mrs. Simpson, and the Simpson family and their need for a banquet lamp.
The man says he has known what it was to do without a banquet lamp himself.
Rebecca estimates that if the Simpsons sell two hundred more cakes this month and next, they can have the lamp by Christmas.
Rebecca adds that the Simpsons can get a shade by summer time, but she may not be able to help much after that day because her aunt Miranda may not like it.
The man says he will take three hundred cakes, which will give the Simpsons shade and all.
Rebecca tips over on her stool and disappears into a clump of lilac bushes, and the man picks her up and brushes her off.
The man advises Rebecca that she should never seem surprised when taking a large order.
Rebecca gives her full name as Rebecca Rowena Randall.
The man remarks that her mother was generous with names, and Rebecca explains her mother could not bear to give up either name.
Rebecca guesses that the man is Mr. Aladdin from the Arabian Nights.
Rebecca asks permission to run down the lane and tell Emma Jane, who must be tired from waiting.
The man nods his assent and Rebecca sped down the lane crying out.
